questions.question: 'No man's land' of the hand refers to the area between the:

options.B: Wrist crease and the distal palmar crease
options.D: Distal palmar crease and the insertion of flexor digitorum superficialis (MCP to PIP region)

questions.explanation: Zone II flexor tendon injuries have a poor outcome because both flexor tendons share a tight sheath.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In forward head posture the muscles that become lengthened and weak are the:

options.A: Deep neck flexors (longus colli and capitis)

questions.explanation: Forward head posture shortens suboccipital muscles, upper trapezius and SCM and lengthens/weakens the deep neck flexors.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which condition is associated with a positive HLA-B27?
questions.explanation: About 90 percent of patients with ankylosing spondylitis are HLA-B27 positive.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Hyperuricaemia with monosodium urate crystals in soft tissues is a feature of:
questions.explanation: Gout is a disorder of purine metabolism with urate crystal deposition.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Raised urinary hydroxyproline and serum alkaline phosphatase are characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Paget's disease has high bone turnover with elevated ALP and hydroxyproline excretion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Wry neck (torticollis) typically presents with:

options.B: Ipsilateral side flexion and contralateral rotation of the neck
options.C: Contralateral side flexion and ipsilateral rotation

questions.explanation: A shortened sternocleidomastoid tilts the head to its own side and rotates the face to the opposite side.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Myositis ossificans most commonly affects the:
questions.explanation: Heterotopic ossification follows contusion of the quadriceps or the brachialis after elbow injury.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Tennis elbow mainly involves which muscle?
questions.explanation: ECRB at the common extensor origin is the commonest site of lateral epicondylitis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Golfer's elbow (medial epicondylitis) mainly involves:

options.C: Flexor carpi radialis and pronator teres

questions.explanation: The common flexor origin, chiefly FCR and pronator teres, is affected.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Ulnar nerve entrapment at the wrist occurs in:
questions.explanation: Guyon's canal is formed by the pisiform and hook of hamate.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Pronator syndrome is median nerve entrapment at the site between:

options.C: The carpal ligament and the wrist bones
options.D: The two heads of pronator teres (and FDS arch)

questions.explanation: In pronator syndrome the median nerve is compressed in the proximal forearm.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Dupuytren's contracture affects the:
questions.explanation: Nodular thickening and contracture of the palmar aponeurosis flexes the ring and little fingers.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Boutonniere deformity results from rupture of the:

options.A: Central slip of the extensor hood

questions.explanation: Loss of the central slip causes PIP flexion and DIP hyperextension.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Boutonniere deformity is characterised by:

options.A: MCP and DIP extension with PIP flexion
options.B: MCP and DIP flexion with PIP extension
options.C: MCP flexion with PIP and DIP extension
options.D: PIP and DIP flexion with MCP extension

questions.explanation: The lateral bands slip volar to the PIP axis, flexing the PIP and hyperextending the DIP.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Swan neck deformity is characterised by:

options.A: MCP and DIP flexion with PIP hyperextension
options.B: PIP and DIP extension with MCP flexion
options.D: MCP and DIP extension with PIP flexion

questions.explanation: Intrinsic tightness and dorsal subluxation of the lateral bands give PIP hyperextension and DIP flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Swan neck deformity is associated with intrinsic muscle contracture and:

options.A: Dorsal subluxation of the lateral extensor bands
options.B: Rupture of the flexor digitorum superficialis only

questions.explanation: Dorsal displacement of the lateral bands over the PIP axis produces PIP hyperextension.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Mallet finger is due to rupture of the extensor tendon at the:
questions.explanation: Loss of terminal tendon extension leaves the DIP flexed.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Gamekeeper's thumb is rupture of the:

options.B: Radial collateral ligament of the first MCP joint
options.C: Ulnar collateral ligament of the first MCP joint

questions.explanation: It follows forced abduction of the thumb MCP joint (e.g. skier's thumb).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Pes planus is characterised by:

options.A: Flattening of the medial longitudinal arch

questions.explanation: In pes planus (flat foot) the medial longitudinal arch is depressed.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In congenital talipes equinovarus (clubfoot) the foot is:
questions.explanation: CTEV has equinus, hindfoot varus and forefoot adduction (cavus).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In hallux valgus the first metatarsal deviates:
questions.explanation: The first metatarsal drifts medially while the great toe deviates laterally.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Spondylolysis is a fracture or defect of the:
questions.explanation: A pars defect produces the 'collar on the Scotty dog' appearance on oblique lumbar X-ray.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The 'Scotty dog sign' on oblique X-ray is associated with:
questions.explanation: A break in the Scottie dog's neck (the pars) indicates spondylolysis.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Rearfoot varus refers to a rigid:
questions.explanation: Rearfoot varus is a structural inversion of the calcaneus relative to the tibia.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Rearfoot valgus refers to a rigid:
questions.explanation: Rearfoot valgus is a structural eversion of the calcaneus.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Genu valgum is commonly known as:
questions.explanation: In genu valgum the knees touch and the ankles are separated.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Genu varum is commonly known as:
questions.explanation: In genu varum the knees are wide apart with the ankles together.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: An increased Q angle predisposes to:
questions.explanation: A larger Q angle increases the lateral pull of the quadriceps on the patella.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Injury to extensor tendon zones 1 and 2 (DIP and middle phalanx) results in a:

options.D: Mallet finger deformity which may progress to swan neck

questions.explanation: Terminal tendon disruption leaves the DIP flexed; unopposed pull on the PIP can develop a swan neck deformity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Injury to extensor tendon zones 3 and 4 (over the PIP joint and proximal phalanx) results in a:
questions.explanation: Central slip disruption gives a boutonniere deformity.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A flexor zone 1 injury (distal to the FDS insertion) involves:
questions.explanation: In zone 1 only the FDP tendon lies beyond the FDS insertion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A flexor zone 2 injury (within the digital sheath, 'no man's land') involves:
questions.explanation: Zone 2 injuries involve both flexor tendons in the tight fibro-osseous sheath.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A flexor zone 3 injury (palm) involves:
questions.explanation: Zone 3 lies between the distal edge of the carpal tunnel and the beginning of the digital sheath, where the lumbricals arise.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Pain felt at the lateral hip is most characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Greater trochanteric pain syndrome causes lateral hip pain aggravated by lying on that side.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In upper crossed syndrome the weak muscles are the:

options.B: Deep neck flexors, rhomboids, serratus anterior and lower trapezius

questions.explanation: Janda's upper crossed syndrome: tight pectorals, upper trapezius, levator scapulae and weak deep neck flexors, rhomboids, serratus anterior, lower trapezius.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In upper crossed syndrome the tight (overactive) muscles are the:

options.B: Pectorals, upper trapezius and levator scapulae

questions.explanation: Tightness of these muscles produces a forward head and rounded shoulders.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common site of neurovascular compression in thoracic outlet syndrome?

options.B: Space between the clavicle and first rib
options.D: Space between pectoralis minor and the thoracic wall

questions.explanation: The common TOS sites are the interscalene triangle, costoclavicular space and subcoracoid (pectoralis minor) space.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In lumbar spinal canal stenosis, spinal ______ increases pain and spinal ______ reduces pain.
questions.explanation: Extension narrows the canal and aggravates symptoms; flexion widens it.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In spondylolisthesis, which position/movement should be avoided?

options.C: Extension, with side flexion and rotation

questions.explanation: Extension and rotation load the pars interarticularis and aggravate slippage.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which investigation is considered the standard for identification of labral tears of the shoulder or hip?
questions.explanation: Arthroscopy gives direct visualisation of the labrum (MR arthrography is the best non-invasive alternative).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: After total hip replacement by the anterolateral approach, the movements to be avoided are:

options.A: Hip flexion beyond 90 degrees, abduction, medial rotation and extension
options.B: Hip flexion beyond 90 degrees, adduction, medial rotation and extension
options.C: Hip flexion beyond 90 degrees, abduction, lateral rotation and extension
options.D: Hip flexion beyond 90 degrees, adduction, lateral rotation and hip extension

questions.explanation: The anterior approach risks anterior dislocation with extension, adduction and external rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: After total hip replacement by the posterolateral approach, the movements to be avoided are:

options.A: Hip flexion beyond 90 degrees, abduction and lateral rotation
options.B: Hip flexion beyond 90 degrees, adduction and medial rotation
options.C: Hip flexion beyond 90 degrees, adduction and lateral rotation
options.D: Hip flexion beyond 90 degrees, abduction and medial rotation

questions.explanation: The posterior approach risks posterior dislocation with flexion, adduction and internal rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Surgery for a scoliotic curve is generally indicated when the Cobb angle is:
questions.explanation: Curves of 25-45 degrees are braced; larger, progressive curves usually need fusion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A T-score of -1 or greater is classified as:
questions.explanation: T-score of -1.0 or above is normal bone density.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A T-score of -2.5 or less is classified as:
questions.explanation: WHO defines osteoporosis as a T-score at or below -2.5.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: A T-score between -1 and -2.5 is classified as:
questions.explanation: Low bone mass lies between -1 and -2.5.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: With ageing, which pattern of bone involvement is seen?

options.C: Trabecular bone is more affected than cortical bone
options.D: Cortical bone is more affected than trabecular bone

questions.explanation: Trabecular bone has a higher turnover and is lost earlier.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In osteoporosis, vertebral compression fractures are most common in the:
questions.explanation: The thoracolumbar junction bears the greatest anterior loading.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Disarticulation of the foot at the midtarsal level is a ______ amputation.
questions.explanation: Chopart's amputation is through the talonavicular and calcaneocuboid joints.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The following are pressure-sensitive areas in a PTB (below-knee) prosthesis EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The patellar tendon is a pressure-tolerant area used to bear weight.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following are pressure-tolerant areas in a PTB socket?

options.B: Patellar tendon, shafts of tibia and fibula, medial tibial plateau

questions.explanation: PTB loading is through the patellar tendon and the muscular soft tissue along the shafts.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: In a transfemoral amputation, the following are pressure-sensitive areas EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The ischial tuberosity is a weight-bearing, pressure-tolerant area in a quadrilateral socket.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which prosthetic foot permits only sagittal plane motion?
questions.explanation: A single-axis ankle gives plantar flexion and dorsiflexion only.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which prosthetic foot permits triplanar motion?
questions.explanation: The stationary-attachment flexible-endoskeleton foot allows motion in all three planes.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which prosthetic foot limits sagittal motion, especially plantar flexion?
questions.explanation: The solid-ankle cushion-heel foot has no articulated ankle; the cushioned heel simulates plantar flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: If the prosthesis is too long, which gait deviations may be seen?
questions.explanation: An over-long prosthesis must be cleared by circumduction, abduction or vaulting on the sound side.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: If the prosthesis is too short, which gait deviation is typically seen?
questions.explanation: A short prosthesis makes the trunk drop towards the prosthetic side.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following can cause forward trunk bending in an amputee during gait?

options.C: All of these: weak quadriceps, hip/knee flexion contracture and an inadequate knee lock

questions.explanation: Forward lean shifts the line of gravity in front of the knee to prevent buckling.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: There will be a forward trunk flexion seen in an amputee during gait if there is:

options.B: Flexion contracture at the hip or reduced strength of hip extensors

questions.explanation: Hip flexion contracture or weak extensors leads to a forward lean.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
